title: Sweep Plan: latency-cost heatmap and QCache presets
content:
Purpose:
This note describes a concrete sweep plan and a small set of recommended default presets for customers and internal presets for the Optimize product. The goal is to produce a compact set of (batching, qcache, quantize) configurations that cover a wide range of cost/latency tradeoffs and can be surfaced as ‘presets’ in the Console and Optimize API.

Context and constraints:
- Targets: short-text chat (avg tokens per response 40–80), long-form generation (avg 250–600), and embeddings (fixed short queries). We care about median latency, p95 tail latency, and per-token cost.
- Hardware: A100-40GB (baseline), T4 for low-cost comparison.
- Models: Llama2-like 13B baseline; 33B for heavier workload. Quantization options are FP16 (baseline), 4-bit PTQ (q4f), and 8-bit dynamic (q8d).
- QCache = prefix-kv cache with TTL eviction; parameters: enabled, max_entries_per_model, ttl_seconds, shard_count.
- Batching knobs: enabled, max_batch_size, max_wait_ms, batching_strategy (latency-first, throughput-first).

Assumptions used in spreadsheet model:
- Per-token GPU cost (baseline A100): $0.000012/token (inference kernel average, accounting amortized infra).
- Quantization reduces per-token GPU cost multiplicatively: q8d x0.7, q4f x0.45 vs FP16 baseline for the 13B family.
- QCache hit ratio depends on workload similarity and prefix length: conservative default hit rates used in model: chat 20% hit (short), long-form 8%, embeddings 0% (no benefit).
- Batching increases throughput but adds headroom latency: latency penalty approximate: 0.6ms per token extra in throughput-first mode at batch sizes >16.

Recommended compact preset grid (3x3 primary cells + one low-latency special):
1) Ultra-low-latency (LL):
   - goal: p50 < 60ms for short chat, p95 < 180ms
   - batch: enabled=false, max_wait_ms=5, max_batch_size=8, batching_strategy=latency-first
   - qcache: enabled=false (consistent latency), ttl_seconds=0, max_entries_per_model=0
   - quant: FP16 (no quantization fallback)
   - when to use: interactive chat, negative-sla-sensitive routes

2) Balanced (B):
   - goal: minimize cost without violating p95 SLO of 500ms for short chat
   - batch: enabled=true, max_wait_ms=15, max_batch_size=32, batching_strategy=latency-first
   - qcache: enabled=true, ttl_seconds=30, max_entries_per_model=10
   - quant: q8d preferred; q4f for dedicated workloads with quality eval pass

3) Cost-optimized (CO):
   - goal: maximize throughput / minimize $/token for high-volume routes with relaxed latency (p95 up to 1.5s)
   - batch: enabled=true, max_wait_ms=60, max_batch_size=128, batching_strategy=throughput-first
   - qcache: enabled=true, ttl_seconds=120, max_entries_per_model=100, shard_count=8
   - quant: q4f default with aggressive per-route quality gating

4) Long-form generation (LF):
   - goal: reduce per-token cost for long sequences (250+ tokens) while controlling total generation time
   - batch: enabled=true, max_wait_ms=30, max_batch_size=64, batching_strategy=throughput-first
   - qcache: enabled=true but conservative (ttl_seconds=45, max_entries_per_model=20) because prefix overlap is smaller
   - quant: q8d baseline; if hallucination/regression detected, fallback to FP16 for the problematic model

Spreadsheet layout (sheet: 'sweep-v1', tabs: workload-defs, sweep-grid, results, heatmaps):
- workload-defs: columns: workload_id, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, qcache_expected_hit, latency_slo_ms
- sweep-grid: rows enumerating each combination with columns: preset_id, batch_enabled, max_wait_ms, max_batch_size, batching_strategy, qcache_enabled, ttl_seconds, max_entries, quant_type, expected_cost_per_1k_tokens, expected_p95_ms
- results: experiment-run rows with real measurements and notes (collected by perf harness)
- heatmaps: pivoted results with median cost vs median latency cells (color scale) and a linked filter for model/hw

Suggested initial sweep matrix (to run on perf harness):
- For each workload (chat_short, chat_long, longform, embeddings):
   - Quant types: FP16, q8d, q4f
   - Batch: max_batch_size in {1, 8, 32, 128} with corresponding max_wait_ms {5, 15, 30, 60}
   - QCache TTL: {0, 15, 60, 300} and max_entries {0, 10, 100}
- Total combinations ~ 4 workloads * 3 quant * 4 batch * 4 qcache_ttl * 3 qcache_entries = 576 baseline combos. We should run a 20% stratified sample first (115 runs) focusing on common combos based on telemetry (chat_short + q8d + 8/32 batch).

Experiment notes / instrumentation requirements:
- Collect per-request: model, hw_type, batch_size_at_dispatch, queue_time_ms, decode_time_ms, kv_cache_hit(boolean), tokens_generated, tokens_requested, p50/p95/p99 latency buckets, GPU utilization, mem footprint
- Tag runs with commit id / kernel config so we can attribute perf deltas to runtime changes
- Run each combo with synthetic and replayed production traces (both steady-state and burst profiles) for at least 30 minutes or 10k requests (whichever first)

Decision heuristics for promoting presets to defaults in Console:
- Minimum data: 3 independent runs with <5% variance in median latency and <8% variance in cost per token across runs
- Quality gate: automated regression check against evaluation prompt set for generation quality. If any metric drop >1.5% ROUGE/BLEU/semantic-sim greater than historical noise, mark as quality-risk and require manual review
- Fallback rules: if q4f shows quality regressions, auto-fallback path in routing: primary= q4f, fallback= q8d, then FP16 if needed. Documented in rollout notes.

Rollback and monitoring runbook (short):
- Monitor: per-route p95, user error-rate, average tokens/req, quality drift alerts from evals, model memory OOMs
- If p95 increases by >2x or user-visible error rate increases by >0.5% within 15m of rollout, auto-rollback to previous preset and open incident L1
- For cost regressions: if $/1k tokens increases by >12% without corresponding latency improvement, flag for optimization review (non-incident)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Empirical mapping for qcache hit rates for our most popular chat apps (need telemetry producer to tag same-session prefixes)
- Memory fragmentation effects for q4f across model families; need to run stress test for 72h to observe slow drift and OOM behavior
- Decide UX shorthand labels and microcopy for Console (e.g., ‘Ultra-low-latency’, ‘Balanced’, ‘Cost-optimized’, plus a ‘Long-form’ route)

Next steps and owner timeline:
- Week 1 (Elena + Eng perf): implement sweep harness parameters and run stratified 20% sample (Nov 10–14)
- Week 2 (Ravi + Maya): full sweep on A100 baseline for top-2 workloads; produce heatmaps and pivoted sheet (Nov 17–21)
- Week 3 (Product + DX): choose 3 presets to expose in Console; prepare short docs + rollout plan (Nov 24–28)

Appendix: quick checklist for experiment run
- [ ] Add tags: workload_id, preset_id, commit_id on perf harness
- [ ] Validate quant kernels available for model family on target HW (binary check)
- [ ] Ensure fallback routing policy test is wired into canary runner
- [ ] Create pivoted heatmap sheet and share with stakeholders

Note: Spreadsheet link in linked_artifacts contains the sweep template and a sample filled run. This doc is a pragmatic starting point — it intentionally trades exhaustive combinatorics for a small set of actionable presets we can validate quickly in the field.

End of memo.
